security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, example snippets, and safe references to environment-variable practices. Semantic review found overbroad authority wording that could cause an agent to treat this project guidance as higher priority than platform, developer, or user instructions.

remediation.issue: Overbroad authority language in the Constitution overview
remediation.suggestion: Replace supreme-priority language with project-scoped guidance, and state that platform, developer, and user instructions remain authoritative.

**Rationale**: Avoid duplication ("不重不漏" principle). Constitution document owns full text, this skil

content.value_statement: Teams need fast access to CC-DevFlow rules without opening the full constitution. This skill summarizes articles, gates, enforcement points, and common decisions.
actual_capabilities: Summarizes all ten CC-DevFlow constitutional articles.
Lists key rules for quality, security, testing, maintainability, and scope control.
Explains Phase -1 Gates for simplicity, anti-abstraction, and integration-first testing.
Maps common implementation questions to constitution articles and recommended actions.
Links readers to the full constitution and related planner agent guidance.
limitations: It does not include the complete constitution text.
It does not execute validation scripts or guardrails.
It depends on referenced project files being present in the workspace.
It reflects CC-DevFlow Constitution v2.0.0 only.

use_cases.title: Check rule coverage before planning
use_cases.description: Review the ten articles and Phase -1 Gates before creating an EPIC or TASKS file.

use_cases.title: Resolve implementation policy questions
use_cases.description: Find quick answers for TODOs, hardcoded secrets, abstractions, TDD order, and scope expansion.

use_cases.title: Prepare focused code reviews
use_cases.description: Use the article summaries to check quality, security, testing, performance, and maintainability expectations.

prompt_templates.title: Find the relevant rule
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner lookup for one policy question.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the DevFlow Constitution quick reference. Which article applies to my question, and what action should I take? Question: [describe your situation].

prompt_templates.title: Check a planned change
prompt_templates.scenario: Review a feature plan before implementation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare this planned change against the Constitution quick reference. List relevant articles, Phase -1 Gates, and any scope risks. Change: [paste summary].

prompt_templates.title: Create a review checklist
prompt_templates.scenario: Turn constitution rules into review criteria.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a concise review checklist from the Constitution quick reference for this pull request. Focus on quality, security, testing, and scope. PR summary: [paste summary].

prompt_templates.title: Audit an EPIC for gate compliance
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning review across multiple gates.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the quick reference to audit this EPIC for Phase -1 compliance. Identify violated gates, missing tests, security concerns, and required corrections. EPIC: [paste text].

output_examples.input: Can I add a TODO and finish it later?
output_examples.output: Relevant rule: Article I.1, No Partial Implementation. Recommended action: complete the implementation now or remove it from scope.

output_examples.input: Should I introduce a BaseController for this small feature?
output_examples.output: Relevant rules: Article II.3 and Article VIII.2. Recommended action: use the framework directly unless repeated needs justify an abstraction.

output_examples.input: Review my EPIC for Phase -1 readiness.
output: Check project count and dependency scope.
Confirm no premature abstractions or generic layers.
Confirm contract and integration tests are planned first.

best_practices: Use the quick reference before planning work, then consult the full constitution for exact wording.
Treat scenario answers as routing guidance, not as a replacement for project-specific review.
Pair each cited article with a concrete action in the current task.
anti_patterns: Using the quick reference as the complete constitution source.
Applying an article without checking the current project scope and requirements.
Bypassing tests, security checks, or scope review because the summary seems sufficient.

faq.question: Does this skill contain the full CC-DevFlow Constitution?
faq.answer: No. It provides article summaries, key rules, examples, enforcement points, and links to the full document.

faq.question: Which Constitution version does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers CC-DevFlow Constitution v2.0.0, effective January 10, 2025.

faq.question: Can it run validation scripts?
faq.answer: No. It names relevant scripts and guardrails, but it does not execute them.

faq.question: Is it useful during planning?
faq.answer: Yes. It summarizes Phase -1 Gates and article requirements that should be checked before EPIC generation.

faq.question: Can developers use it during code review?
faq.answer: Yes. It helps reviewers connect quality, security, testing, and scope concerns to specific articles.

faq.question: What should I do when the summary is not enough?
faq.answer: Open the linked full constitution and related agent files for complete requirements and enforcement details.
